subject: Kiosk offline lead-sync (SFTP + HubSpot field mapping)
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara@leadsnap.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Lead capture for Redwood booth — offline kiosk + sync options

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the quick chat earlier. Per our notes: LeadSnap can run the badge scanner app in fully offline mode (local store-and-forward) and then push CSV batches to an SFTP endpoint at the end of each day. Questions we need answered to size the integration and delivery timeline: 

- Expected daily lead volume (est. unique badges / day) for your marquee events (you gave 3k/day as a peak number)
- Required HubSpot fields (we can include the standard set + two custom fields)
- Consent language you plan to show on the kiosk (we have a default GDPR/US opt-in template)
- Whether you need immediate streaming for high-touch prospects (we can do a webhook path for those)

We attached a short spec (LeadSnap_kiosk_spec_v3.pdf) and a sample consent text (consent_text_v2.txt).

If you can confirm the HubSpot field mapping and whether you prefer SFTP or webhook for the daily feed, we’ll produce a test CSV and SFTP filename conventions.

Cheers,
Sara Lim
Lead Operations
LeadSnap Media

(attachment: LeadSnap_kiosk_spec_v3.pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara@leadsnap.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lead capture for Redwood booth — offline kiosk + sync options

Thanks Sara — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volume: plan for 2,500 unique badges/day typical, 5,000/day peak.
- HubSpot: We want the following fields in the CSV: email, first_name, last_name, company, job_title, phone, event_id, booth_id, scan_time (UTC), consent_flag, source_campaign. Two custom fields: event_id and consent_flag.
- Consent: we need explicit consent text for both EU and US; Laura I’ve looped you for the final legal-approved wording.
- SFTP vs webhook: prefer SFTP nightly batch for the main file (reduces rate limits). For leads flagged as "high interest" (checkbox on kiosk), we want a webhook to our CS queue for immediate follow-up. 

Can you confirm your filename pattern and whether you can include a hash/dedupe key (e.g., email+scan_time) as an exported column? Also we’ll need a test file by next Tue (2026-04-14) so our ops team can validate mapping.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Field Marketing Manager | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara@leadsnap.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lead capture for Redwood booth — offline kiosk + sync options

Sara — quick note on consent language. For this event we need two short variants: 

1) EU (GDPR) variant: "By providing your badge scan, you consent to Redwood Inference and its trusted partners processing your contact data for event follow-up and product updates. You can withdraw consent at any time. See our Privacy Policy: https://redwood.com/privacy."

2) US/ROW variant: "I agree to receive communications from Redwood Inference about product updates and events. Message and data rates may apply. See our Privacy Policy: https://redwood.com/privacy."

We want the kiosk to surface the correct variant based on a simple country selection dropdown — please confirm you can support this and store consent_flag as "gdpr_eu" or "consent_us".

Also, HubSpot field mappings we prefer (CSV header -> HubSpot property):
- email -> email
- first_name -> firstname
- last_name -> lastname
- company -> company
- job_title -> jobtitle
- phone -> phone
- event_id -> custom_event_id
- booth_id -> custom_booth_id
- scan_time -> hs_timestamp
- consent_flag -> custom_consent_flag
- source_campaign -> source

Please include an additional column dedupe_key that is md5(email + scan_time) so we can dedupe on ingest.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Ops Program Manager | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Alex Reed <alex@eventops.co>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lim <sara@leadsnap.io>, leadsnap-ops@leadsnap.io
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Lead capture for Redwood booth — offline kiosk + sync options

Thanks Ben/Laura — quick technical reply from the LeadSnap ops side: 

- Filename convention: REDWOOD_EVT-{event_id}-{YYYYMMDD}-HHMMSS.csv (e.g. REDWOOD_EVT-114-20260414-235900.csv)
- Dedupe: we can include dedupe_key as md5(email + scan_time) in the export. If email is missing we add a placeholder and include badge_id as fallback.
- Country-based consent: kiosk supports geo dropdown and will write consent_flag exactly as asked (gdpr_eu / consent_us).
- Offline store-and-forward: app keeps encrypted local SQLite queue for up to 7 days; if SFTP fails it retries every 30 minutes.
- Webhook for high-interest: yes — we can fire a POST with full JSON payload to your CS webhook (please share endpoint and auth).

Attached: SFTP_instructions.txt with recommended private key setup and an example test CSV. We will upload a formal test file to the Drive link by EOD Mon (2026-04-14).

Alex Reed
Integration Lead | EventOps (on behalf of LeadSnap)
(attachment: SFTP_instructions.txt)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reed <alex@eventops.co>, Sara Lim <sara@leadsnap.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 13:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lead capture for Redwood booth — offline kiosk + sync options

Appreciate the detail. A couple of technical asks from our side before we ingest the first test: 

1) Can the CSV include a version header row with schema_version e.g. "v1.2" so we can quickly detect schema changes.
2) Timestamp format must be ISO 8601 in UTC (e.g., 2026-04-14T23:59:00Z).
3) For dedupe, we want md5 as lower-case hex and include both dedupe_key and source_id (LeadSnap device id).
4) Please remove personally-identifiable badge images from the export; we only need badge_id if email is absent.

If you can confirm these, we’ll spin up an SFTP test user and drop credentials to the ops channel (we prefer key-based auth). Also, please include a 50-row sample CSV so we can run HubSpot mapping and SFDC sync tests.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Platform Integrations | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Sara Lim <sara@leadsnap.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Reed <alex@eventops.co>, leadsnap-ops@leadsnap.io
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Lead capture for Redwood booth — offline kiosk + sync options

All good — we’ll deliver per the specs: 

- Schema header: schema_version= v1.2 included as first CSV row.
- Timestamps: ISO 8601 UTC.
- dedupe_key: md5(email+scan_time) lower-case + source_id column.
- No images in export; badge_id only when email missing.

We uploaded a 50-row test CSV to the Drive link above and attached SFTP instructions. Also sending a DocuSign link for a small SLA (turnaround for nightly uploads + support SLA) — please have legal review and sign. Target: validate ingestion by Thu 2026-04-16 and finish UAT by Fri 2026-04-17.

Let us know the webhook endpoint for high-interest leads and we’ll enable streaming for the checkboxes flagged on the kiosk.

Thanks — Sara
Lead Operations | LeadSnap Media
(attachments: sample_50_rows.csv, SFTP_instructions.txt, consent_text_v2.txt)
